title: Coplanar WASP-105 trials reach close approaches at giant eccentricity 0.5 but remain clear through 0.3
abstract: We test the proposed 2.002808-day inner planet at WASP-105 with Newtonian integrations. We assume that it orbits the same 0.89-solar-mass star as the 1.8-Jupiter-mass giant. In 168 coplanar 200-year trials with an initially circular inner orbit, all 96 starts at giant eccentricities from 0 to 0.3 remain clear of the distance and orbit-change flags. At eccentricity 0.4, 15 of 24 starts remain clear; at 0.5 and 0.6, none do. The tested inner masses are 1, 5, and 25 Earth masses. A flag means a close approach or a large orbit change, not a demonstrated collision. All twelve adaptive-integrator checks agree on the flag status. Eight representative starts at eccentricities up to 0.3 remain clear for 2,000 years. Four of 24 separate 200-year states on a fixed-angular-momentum track reach a close approach, all at the tested eccentricity 0.9. The null results at 0.97 do not prove long-term safety. The present circular separation is 9.87 mutual Hill radii, but the local periastron gap along that track falls to 2.53 in the high-eccentricity limit. The circular inner and giant paths still do not cross in that limit. These are conditional calculations, not planet confirmation or a measured eccentricity bound. We do not simulate tides or a continuous migration history. The package contains original code, all simulated trials, analytic checks, provenance, and figures. No external raw records are bundled.
